stemBlocks.value: Think first: Look for two numbers that multiply to the constant term and add to the coefficient of x.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p093-q14 from workbook page 93.

solutionSteps.instruction: Look for two numbers with product 24 and sum 11.

contentBlocks.value: Factor pairs of 24: 1 and 24, 2 and 12, 3 and 8, 4 and 6
Both numbers are positive, so both signs are plus

strategyBlocks.value: List the factor pairs of 24, pick the pair adding to 11, and write the two brackets.

whyThisWorks.value: Expanding (x + p)(x + q) gives x² + (p + q)x + pq, so for a quadratic beginning with x² the constant term is the product of the two numbers and the middle coefficient is their sum. Listing the factor pairs of the constant is therefore a complete search rather than guesswork.

commonErrors.misconception: Choosing numbers that add to 24 and multiply to 11.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Choosing numbers that add to 24 and multiply to 11.

commonErrors.misconception: Missing a factor pair and concluding the expression will not factorise.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Missing a factor pair and concluding the expression will not factorise.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing (x + 6)(x + 4), whose middle term is 10x, without checking.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing (x + 6)(x + 4), whose middle term is 10x, without checking.

examTip.value: List every factor pair of the constant term in order — you will find the right pair faster than by trial and error.
